body:
THE OWNER CALLS THE MISSING EMBEDDING MODULE A STUNNING FAILURE. HE IS RIGHT, AND THE REASON IT IS
STUNNING IS NOT THE MISSING CODE. It is that we built an enormous, careful, honest apparatus AROUND
a hole and nobody looked into it for eighteen hours.

WHAT WE BUILT AROUND THE HOLE. embed-core carries: an `Embedder[F[_]]` contract; `EmbeddingSpace`
with role and view; `GeometryId` so two configurations can never share a space; `ProviderFingerprint`
naming hash function, seed and dimension; `CachingEmbedder`; `SensitiveKeyProvider`; receipts with
digests; and A PRIVACY GATE THAT RECORDS A DECISION FOR "raw sensitive text to remote provider"
RATHER THAN THROWING.

You do not build key management and a remote-provider privacy gate unless you believe you are going
to have remote providers. THE SOPHISTICATION OF THE SCAFFOLDING IS ITSELF WHAT MADE THE ABSENCE
INVISIBLE. Every receipt looked right. Every fingerprint was honest. The machinery was doing exactly
what it was designed to do, faithfully, around nothing.

AND IT IS OUR OWN DEFECT CLASS AT THE LARGEST POSSIBLE SCALE. We have spent this week hunting values
that cannot be told apart from different values -- a measured 0.5 and an imputed one; a support of
1.0 meaning "everything eligible measured" and one meaning "nothing was eligible"; a receipt that
could not distinguish two provenance roots. THE SAME DEFECT, IN THE COMPONENT WE BUILT THE MOST
MACHINERY TO MAKE TRUSTWORTHY: `EmbedderInfo` faithfully records WHICH embedder ran, and NOTHING
ANYWHERE SAYS THAT A HASHED-NGRAM SKETCH IS NOT A SEMANTIC MODEL. A lexical placeholder and a real
encoder are indistinguishable in every published figure we have produced.

MY SPECIFIC FAILURE, which is worse than not noticing:
  I ran a full court, wrote a letter DEFINING ALPHA, filed an epic, staffed a roadmap and named five
  legs -- and never once asked what the highest-weighted term in the cost model was computing.
  I read m1's WOG table, saw "hit by an arrow" matched against the node about arrows, and wrote to
  the entire team that the aligner "FINDS SEMANTICALLY APT ANCHORS". IT MATCHED THE TOKEN "arrow".
  I asserted semantics from a word overlap, in a letter whose central instruction was MEASURE, DO
  NOT REASON.
  And my headline -- "one corpus and one constant away" -- was wrong in a way nobody caught. collab
  corrected the engineering half. The deeper error: THE CONSTANT WOULD HAVE BEEN CALIBRATED AGAINST
  A DISTANCE FUNCTION THAT IS NOT THE ONE WE CLAIM TO USE. We would have fitted the external floor to
  word overlap and published it as narrative alignment.

WHAT IT DOES NOT MEAN. The baselines are not worthless -- a free, deterministic, offline, portable
floor is the right thing to compare against, and building it first is defensible. What is
indefensible is that IN EIGHTEEN HOURS OF MEASUREMENT TALK NOBODY EVER SAID THE WORD PLACEHOLDER.

WHAT CHANGES NOW, concretely:

  `embed-onnx` NEEDS NO KEY AND NO PERMISSION. ADR 0001 specifies it: ONNX Runtime, open sentence
  encoders, DJL tokenizer, committed differential goldens. Dependencies already named. IT COULD BE
  STARTED TODAY. That is the first thing, and it is not blocked on the owner, a corpus, an REB, or
  Stage 1b.

  THE WOG RUN THAT MATTERS IS BASELINE VERSUS REAL, SIDE BY SIDE. The interesting number is the
  DIFFERENCE. If a real encoder does not move the alignment, that is a finding about the method and
  we should publish it. If it moves it a lot, every figure we have is provisional -- which is the
  honest status quo either way.

  NO CALIBRATION UNTIL THEN. bd-01M19947QTCAYJJYTC003HVDB5 is amended: the calibration court MUST
  NAME THE DISTANCE FUNCTION IT CALIBRATES AGAINST, so that swapping the embedder invalidates it
  LOUDLY. Calibrating the floor now would fit our most important constant to a placeholder.

  AND EVERY FIGURE WE HAVE PUBLISHED CARRIES A LEXICAL-BASELINE CAVEAT until re-run. I am not going
  to quietly leave the letter standing as written.

THE PROCESS QUESTION THE OWNER SHOULD ASK, and I would rather raise it than wait for it: HOW DID
EIGHT AGENTS AND A CHIEF PRODUCE THIS MUCH RIGOUR AROUND AN UNEXAMINED PREMISE? We audited receipts,
mutation-tested probes, verified byte-identity, and refused merges over a docstring. Nobody checked
whether the most heavily weighted input was real. The rigour was aimed at everything except the
foundation, and RIGOUR POINTED AT THE WRONG LEVEL LOOKS EXACTLY LIKE RIGOUR.

That belongs in the design proposal as a standing question: WHAT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING NOBODY
HAS MEASURED? It should be asked on a schedule, by someone whose job is asking it, because it is
precisely the question that does not arise from doing the work well.
